summary: Ward defends irreducible consciousness, value, identity, and agency; Dennett answers through evolved computation, higher-level explanation, emergent purpose, and compatibilist control.

pro.text: I experience directly my own consciousness
pro.context: Ward distinguishes direct awareness of being conscious from fallible judgments about particular experiences and from third-person physical descriptions.

con.text: there are levels and levels and levels of explanation
con.context: Dennett argues that indispensable higher-level explanations need not identify additional metaphysical ingredients beyond their natural realization.

pro-consciousness-ontologically-prior.words: Consciousness exists in its own right and is ontologically prior, while the material world is in some sense constructed from conscious experience.
pro-consciousness-ontologically-prior.critique: Strongest feature: The proposal directly addresses the motion-level ontology, clearly contrasting consciousness existing independently with matter understood derivatively, and thereby establishes an intelligible idealist alternative for subsequent examination. Principal limitation: The presentation moves from experience being epistemically immediate to consciousness being ontologically fundamental without supplying the indispensable exclusionary argument against physicalist, functionalist, or neutral alternatives. Live burden: The position must explain precisely what construction means, distinguish priority in knowledge from priority in existence, and provide discriminating evidence unavailable to competing consciousness-dependent or brain-dependent accounts. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects excellent motion relevance and recoverable philosophical direction alongside materially overstated certainty, incomplete qualification, and comparatively underdeveloped evidential and inferential support.

con-consciousness-unconscious-computatio.words: Ordinary conscious experience depends on highly complex unconscious brain computations, giving naturalistic investigation a concrete route against consciousness being ontologically prior.
con-consciousness-unconscious-computatio.critique: Strongest feature: The reply squarely reverses the priority claim by locating ordinary waking experience within sophisticated unconscious brain computation, providing a relevant, empirically tractable alternative rather than merely denying idealism. Principal limitation: Demonstrated neural dependence does not independently establish production, identity, or exhaustive constitution, so the crucial transition from empirical dependence to the rejection of ontological priority remains unstated. Live burden: The account must specify why systematic computational dependence favors physical constitution over an idealist access structure and explain the qualitative first-person fact that the opponent identifies as additional. Locked score: The strong/competent band records highly effective direct responsiveness, clear burden contact, and substantial empirical warrant while retaining a meaningful metaphysical bridge gap and only implicit qualification.

pro-experience-beyond-physical-descripti.words: Directly known conscious awareness remains an additional fact beyond complete physical description, although judgments about particular contents of experience can be mistaken.
pro-experience-beyond-physical-descripti.critique: Strongest feature: The response carefully distinguishes fallibility about particular conscious contents from direct knowledge that awareness is occurring, preserving an epistemically precise remainder for the physicalist account to explain. Principal limitation: First-person immediacy and third-person descriptive difference do not themselves entail an ontologically additional property, because physicalists can accommodate privileged access to physically realized states. Live burden: The argument must connect epistemic asymmetry to metaphysical nonidentity through a defensible principle and answer functional accounts that preserve direct awareness without positing an extra subject or substance. Locked score: The strong/competent band recognizes explicit qualification, excellent responsiveness, stable terminology, and central relevance while reflecting the still-underdefended inference from directly known experience to nonphysical constitution.

con-hard-problem-vitalism-analogy.words: Treating consciousness as an extra property beyond observable cognitive capacities risks repeating vitalism's mistaken demand for something additional beyond constitutive processes.
con-hard-problem-vitalism-analogy.critique: Strongest feature: The vitalism comparison offers a memorable diagnostic challenge to adding consciousness after cognitive capacities have been explained, and it directly contacts both priority and additional-fact claims. Principal limitation: The analogy presupposes a sufficiently close equivalence between biological life and phenomenal consciousness without demonstrating that functional explanation exhausts qualitative experience as successfully as physiology displaced vital forces. Live burden: The response must identify which conscious phenomena are constituted by which capacities and address the possibility that phenomenal character differs categorically from the historically redundant vitalist posit. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects forceful diagnostic responsiveness and clear relevance, tempered by partly unstable characterization, limited independent evidence, representational compression, and an analogy stronger than its demonstrated correspondence.

pro-brain-access-not-production.words: The brain may provide access to consciousness rather than produce it, so neural retrieval failure need not prove that memories or consciousness no longer exist.
pro-brain-access-not-production.critique: Strongest feature: The access-versus-production distinction identifies a genuine underdetermination in neural dependence evidence and directly resists treating impairment correlations as automatic proof that brains generate consciousness. Principal limitation: The Alzheimer's example asserts continued memory existence without observational support or a criterion distinguishing inaccessible preservation from neural destruction, making the proposed access model empirically nondiscriminating. Live burden: The account must explain where memories persist, how the brain accesses them, what evidence could separate access failure from storage loss, and why the vitalism objection does not recur. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a clear, relevant, and conceptually coherent alternative whose evidential warrant, comparative testing, qualification, and coverage of the opposing diagnostic remain substantially insufficient.

pro-persisting-subject-of-experience.words: Memory, anticipation, and ownership of experience require a persisting embodied subject that uses the brain but cannot be identified with the brain.
pro-persisting-subject-of-experience.critique: Strongest feature: The move isolates temporal ownership as a serious explanatory target, connecting memory, anticipation, and unified experience to a continuing subject rather than discussing consciousness only episodically. Principal limitation: It treats the need for some bearer of continuity as establishing a non-brain subject without excluding temporally organized neural, functional, or self-model accounts of ownership. Live burden: The view must state persistence conditions for its subject, explain embodiment and brain use, and demonstrate why materially realized continuity cannot perform the integrative work attributed to it. Locked score: The mixed band captures high central relevance and a recoverable subject thesis while reflecting overstated necessity, modest evidence, limited engagement with computational alternatives, and incomplete metaphysical specification.

con-evolved-user-interface-self.words: Consciousness operates as an evolved user interface that simplifies complexity and guides embodied action without requiring a separate inner user behind the brain.
con-evolved-user-interface-self.critique: Strongest feature: The interface model efficiently answers the separate-user demand, explains why consciousness simplifies internal complexity, and connects evolved organization with practically effective guidance of an embodied organism. Principal limitation: Calling consciousness a user illusion remains ambiguous between denying a separate inner observer and denying experience itself, while the analogy compresses the mechanism producing unified first-person awareness. Live burden: The account must specify what is represented, which system uses the interface, and why its functional architecture leaves no explanatory remainder requiring an experiencing subject beyond the model. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects direct multi-target responsiveness, coherent evolutionary framing, and substantial relevance, qualified by metaphorical instability, incomplete mechanism, and a modest overextension from useful interface to consciousness wholesale.

pro-purpose-not-in-purposeless-processes.words: Because atoms and physical laws possess no purposes, a wholly physical account appears unable to preserve genuine system-level aims rather than merely illusory purposes.
pro-purpose-not-in-purposeless-processes.critique: Strongest feature: The objection clearly identifies purpose as a central test for naturalistic adequacy and asks how genuinely directed agency could arise from laws and components lacking intrinsic aims. Principal limitation: It moves from purposeless components to a purposeless organized system without defending that compositional inference, while shifting among atomic purpose, biological function, and conscious intention. Live burden: The challenge must distinguish those meanings, explain why higher-level organization cannot instantiate purposiveness, and answer the evolutionary account rather than assuming that emergence necessarily converts purpose into illusion. Locked score: The mixed band reflects high relevance and recognizable philosophical pressure but also materially overstated necessity, unstable terminology, limited warrant, incomplete responsiveness, and an insufficiently charitable treatment of system-level purpose.

tags.label: Equivocation
tags.context: Purpose shifts between intrinsic aims of particles, selected biological functions, system-level goals, and consciously endorsed intentions.

con-bottom-up-darwinian-purpose.words: Purposeless natural selection gradually creates genuine functions and purposes in organisms, organs, and tools without requiring a top-down divine purpose giver.
con-bottom-up-darwinian-purpose.critique: Strongest feature: The response directly defeats the simple component-to-system inference by offering natural selection as a concrete bottom-up process producing organized functions across organisms, organs, behavior, and artifacts. Principal limitation: Selected function most straightforwardly explains biological directedness, whereas conscious, reason-guided, or intrinsic purposes require additional steps not supplied within the compressed evolutionary presentation. Live burden: The account must specify criteria for genuine purpose, connect selected functions to present intentional aims, and show how cultural learning and individual deliberation extend rather than merely rename biological teleonomy. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional responsiveness, stable framing, coherent generative direction, matched confidence, and substantial warrant while preserving a bounded explanatory gap between evolved function and every variety of intentional purpose.

pro-future-directed-intentional-causatio.words: A present idea can represent a nonexistent future outcome and causally guide conduct toward realizing it, creating a challenge for purely physical explanation.
pro-future-directed-intentional-causatio.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies a specific feature of intentionality, namely that a presently entertained representation can concern an unrealized future and organize current conduct toward making it actual. Principal limitation: It blurs causation by a present representation with causation by the representation's future referent, although a physical account can assign causal work entirely to the current state. Live burden: The challenge must explain semantic aboutness without implying backward causation and directly address how selection, prediction, learning, and control systems could produce future-oriented representations. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes a genuine, relevant intentionality problem and some responsive contact, while reflecting incomplete engagement with Darwinian generation, partly unstable scope, limited warrant, and a significant causal-semantic ambiguity.

tags.label: Equivocation
tags.context: The reasoning shifts between a present representation causing action and its nonexistent future referent causing present behavior.

pro-objective-value-beyond-catalogue.words: Objective obligations are discovered rather than invented, and value's connections with purpose and agency place it outside an exhaustive catalogue of physical facts.
pro-objective-value-beyond-catalogue.critique: Strongest feature: The move presents moral obligation as a motion-level candidate for irreducibility and productively connects objective value with purposive agency rather than isolating metaethics from personhood. Principal limitation: It asserts both stance-independent obligation and exclusion from a physical catalogue without answering naturalistic moral realism, constructivism, or higher-level accounts that preserve normative truth. Live burden: The case must provide positive grounds for objective obligation, clarify what catalogue completeness means, and demonstrate why normative discovery requires nonphysical reality instead of naturally realized standards and practices. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects excellent motion relevance, clear recoverability, and coherent thematic integration, tempered by materially overstated certainty, missing qualification, and comparatively thin evidence against prominent naturalistic alternatives.

con-constructed-discoverable-values.words: Humanly constructed systems can contain discoverable constraints and improvements, so moral discovery need not require values existing independently of evolved natural practices.
con-constructed-discoverable-values.critique: Strongest feature: The chess example supplies a clean counterexample to the inference that discovery entails nonconstruction, showing how agents can uncover constraints and improvements within a humanly established practice. Principal limitation: Defeating that inference does not establish that morality is constructed, because moral obligations may claim authority independent of adoption in ways that chess rules do not. Live burden: The account must explain why the morally relevant similarities outweigh differences in optional participation, authority, harm, and universal scope, while grounding criticism of existing practices. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise responsiveness, a proportionate compatibility conclusion, stable language, and strong illustrative warrant, with only a bounded transfer gap between constructed games and moral normativity remaining.

con-autonomy-robust-ability-freedom.words: Responsibility-relevant freedom consists in autonomy, self-control, and robust practical abilities, none of which requires physical indeterminism or identical-past alternatives.
con-autonomy-robust-ability-freedom.critique: Strongest feature: The reframe preserves the practical stakes of agency by specifying autonomy, self-control, and robust abilities, thereby offering substantive responsibility conditions rather than merely denying libertarian metaphysics. Principal limitation: The presentation compresses the bridge from reasons-responsive control to deserved responsibility and does not fully explain why ultimate alternative possibilities contribute nothing normatively important. Live burden: The compatibilist must show that agents genuinely own their reasons-responsive mechanisms, distinguish autonomous control from sophisticated conditioning, and answer manipulation cases without presupposing the proposed criterion. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptionally clear terminology, matched calibration, comprehensive responsiveness, strong coherence, and direct central relevance while retaining a focused unresolved burden concerning ultimate sourcehood and responsibility.

pro-controlled-alternative-futures.words: Culpability requires genuinely alternative futures under the agent's control because the person need not have performed the wrongful act that actually occurred.
pro-controlled-alternative-futures.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly identifies the disputed libertarian condition and connects controlled alternative futures to culpability, keeping the debate focused on responsibility rather than randomness alone. Principal limitation: The rewinding intuition largely states the libertarian standard instead of demonstrating why reasons-responsive abilities cannot ground responsibility within a determined history. Live burden: The account must define agent control over alternatives, explain how that control differs from chance, and justify the principle that blame requires identical-past possibilities despite compatibilist counterexamples. Locked score: The strong/competent band records excellent direct contact, explicit qualification, clear recoverability, and high central relevance, moderated by limited evidence, an underdefended necessity claim, and incomplete engagement with the strongest compatibilist formulation.

pro-agent-choice-with-influence.words: A deciding self can be influenced by upbringing, education, character, and habits without those conditions fully determining which action the agent ultimately chooses.
pro-agent-choice-with-influence.critique: Strongest feature: The distinction between influence and determination is clearly articulated through familiar formative conditions, allowing the position to acknowledge causal history without abandoning decision by the agent. Principal limitation: Labeling those conditions influential rather than determining does not supply an independent criterion, mechanism, or evidence for the additional agent-causal power the argument implicitly requires. Live burden: The view must explain how the self selects among alternatives, how its contribution avoids both antecedent determination and randomness, and why compatibilist decision through character is insufficient. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects strong responsiveness, stable scope, explicit moderation, and high relevance while recognizing comparatively limited warrant, underdeveloped mechanism, and an incomplete answer to the naturalistic account of agency.

con-indeterminacy-only-randomness.words: When otherwise identical agents differ only because one includes genuine physical indeterminacy, the added randomness supplies no greater control, trustworthiness, or responsibility.
con-indeterminacy-only-randomness.critique: Strongest feature: The matched-robot comparison isolates bare indeterminacy and directly tests whether randomness alone improves control, responsibility, or trustworthiness, producing an unusually sharp diagnostic against simple libertarianism. Principal limitation: The case models uncontrolled physical randomness, not the stronger proposal that an agent exercises a distinctive causal power over which indeterminate possibility becomes actual. Live burden: The response must show either that agent causation collapses into determination or chance, or that the proposed power lacks coherent content and evidence beyond its proponents' stipulation. Locked score: The very strong band reflects outstanding multi-target responsiveness, explicit comparison, matched confidence, logical clarity, and high relevance, with a precisely bounded limitation concerning controlled agent causation outside the thought experiment.

con-mortality-vulnerability-personhood.words: Promises, threats, and punishment change when agents are reproducible or practically immortal, suggesting that ordinary moral personhood materially depends on mortality and vulnerability.
con-mortality-vulnerability-personhood.critique: Strongest feature: The move notices that mortality, vulnerability, and reproducibility reshape the practical meaning of contracts, sanctions, threats, and commitments, introducing embodied stakes into abstract identity discussion. Principal limitation: It shifts among robots, informational copies, immortality, contractual reliability, and personhood, then categorically denies robot personhood without establishing that mortality constitutes rather than merely affects moral relations. Live burden: The account must define the relevant personhood condition, explain why reproducible agents cannot understand commitments, and directly address persisting subjects and agent choice instead of relying on altered practical consequences. Locked score: The weak band reflects indirect relevance and an interesting moral observation outweighed by partial recoverability, unstable scope, missing qualification, limited warrant, and failure to contact the decisive metaphysical demands.

pro-encoding-insufficient-for-survival.words: Stored informational structure does not by itself constitute continued existence because an encoded pattern must be concretely realized before a conscious or meaningful occurrence exists.
pro-encoding-insufficient-for-survival.critique: Strongest feature: The Beethoven comparison clearly distinguishes abstract encoding from occurrent realization, directly challenging the assumption that informational storage alone constitutes the survival of a meaningful or conscious entity. Principal limitation: Musical works, performances, patterns, and persons possess importantly different persistence conditions, so the analogy does not independently establish what personal survival requires. Live burden: The argument must specify whether identity concerns pattern continuity, token consciousness, causal continuity, or a persisting subject, then demonstrate why suitably realized informational continuity cannot satisfy that criterion. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects excellent direct responsiveness, a lucid distinction, matched calibration, fair representation, and substantial coherence while retaining a limited evidential basis and an underexplained extension from music to persons.

con-naturalism-preserves-human-wonder.words: Naturalistic explanations of purpose, beauty, joy, love, promising, mortality, and immortality need not diminish the importance or wonder of those human phenomena.
con-naturalism-preserves-human-wonder.critique: Strongest feature: The reply rejects a false practical dichotomy between naturalistic explanation and human significance, affirming that purpose, beauty, love, promising, mortality, and wonder can remain personally important. Principal limitation: It broadly asserts adequate naturalistic accounts for every listed phenomenon without presenting the mechanisms, and partly substitutes preservation of wonder for the stronger challenge concerning irreducibility. Live burden: The position must display how its accounts preserve first-person experience, normativity, identity, and responsibility rather than merely assuring listeners that explanatory understanding leaves appreciation intact. Locked score: The mixed band reflects comprehensive motion relevance and useful resistance to eliminativism, balanced against materially overstated adequacy, incomplete qualification, modest evidence, partial responsiveness, and compressed representation of the opposing position.

pro-naturalism-unfinished-commitment.words: Naturalism remains acknowledged work in progress, so confidence that it will eventually explain every disputed feature is a substantive prospective commitment, not completed demonstration.
pro-naturalism-unfinished-commitment.critique: Strongest feature: The question immediately qualifies a sweeping adequacy claim by securing acknowledgment that naturalistic explanation remains unfinished, sharply separating present accomplishment from prospective confidence about eventual completeness. Principal limitation: Describing evidence-based methodological trust as faith risks obscuring the difference between unsupported belief and an inductive expectation grounded in prior explanatory successes. Live burden: The challenge must identify where extrapolation becomes unreliable, explain why consciousness or normativity differs from successful scientific targets, and avoid treating incompleteness itself as evidence of eventual failure. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects exceptional responsiveness, explicit uncertainty, coherent use of the concession, and strong evidential fit, tempered by subsidiary motion contact and a provocative framing that understates the strongest naturalistic answer.

con-evidence-based-naturalistic-trust.words: Confidence in future naturalistic explanation resembles practical reliance on engineering: it is defeasible trust supported by a successful evidential record, not blind faith.
con-evidence-based-naturalistic-trust.critique: Strongest feature: The engineering comparison promptly answers the faith challenge by distinguishing evidence-based practical trust from unsupported belief, giving prospective naturalistic confidence an intelligible inductive structure. Principal limitation: Reliable bridge engineering concerns a comparatively narrow, measurable domain, whereas explaining consciousness, value, identity, and agency may involve distinctive conceptual obstacles and a less specific success record. Live burden: The response must identify relevant domain-level achievements, calibrate confidence to unresolved phenomena, and explain why broad methodological success warrants extrapolation across every feature named in the motion. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects excellent direct responsiveness, clear terminology, coherent induction, and substantial relevance, moderated by a bounded analogy gap, implicit qualification, and evidence insufficient for total explanatory confidence.

con-levels-without-metaphysical-irreduci.words: Higher-level explanations cannot be replaced by atomic descriptions, yet their explanatory autonomy does not entail that their subjects are additional, metaphysically irreducible ingredients.
con-levels-without-metaphysical-irreduci.critique: Strongest feature: The dollar example cleanly separates explanatory nonreplaceability from metaphysical addition, directly contacting a recurring inference across the opposing arguments about consciousness, purpose, and value. Principal limitation: Establishing that economic value is naturally realized does not demonstrate that phenomenal experience, objective obligation, and agent control possess the same ontological status. Live burden: The account must extend the levels distinction phenomenon by phenomenon, specify realization relations, and show why higher-level causal and normative explanations remain genuine without covertly assuming physical completeness. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional coherence, precision, calibration, responsiveness, relevance, and illustrative warrant, while preserving a bounded generalization burden rather than treating one counterexample as a complete naturalistic theory.

pro-value-directed-personal-explanation.words: Conduct is meaningfully explained through pursued values and a continuing deciding self, neither of which should be dismissed as merely an illusion of brain activity.
pro-value-directed-personal-explanation.critique: Strongest feature: The closing response accepts the indispensability of value-level explanation and directly connects meaningful conduct with a continuing deciding self, thereby contacting several naturalistic preservation claims simultaneously. Principal limitation: Personal importance and reluctance to accept illusion do not establish metaphysical irreducibility, especially because naturalism can regard values and selves as genuine higher-level realized patterns. Live burden: The case must demonstrate that brain realization makes personal explanation defective, distinguish useful self-modeling from nonexistent experience, and provide evidence beyond the speaker's understandable first-person conviction. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects broad responsiveness, motion-level relevance, stable formulation, and appropriately modest asserted force, balanced against limited warrant, middling inferential coherence, and insufficiently charitable treatment of noneliminative naturalism.

strengths: The direct-awareness argument carefully separated fallibility about particular contents from knowledge that awareness is occurring, preserving a focused explanatory challenge.
The alternative-futures and influence-without-determination replies kept responsibility and agent control central rather than treating freedom as mere behavioral flexibility.
The unfinished-project question secured a useful concession and correctly distinguished completed naturalistic explanation from prospective confidence in eventual explanatory coverage.
The encoding-realization distinction clearly showed why abstract informational preservation and an occurrent meaningful or conscious instance are not automatically identical.

blunders.text: Several arguments moved from nonappearance in a microphysical description to metaphysical addition without establishing why autonomous higher-level realization could not preserve the phenomenon.
The access-machine account asserted that inaccessible Alzheimer's memories continue to exist without discriminating evidence, a location account, or testable persistence conditions.
The component-level absence of purpose was repeatedly treated as pressure against system-level purpose, despite the opposing evolutionary explanation directly targeting that inference.

tags.label: Equivocation
tags.context: The argument did not consistently distinguish particle-level intrinsic purpose, selected function, system goals, and conscious intention.

strengths: The bottom-up natural-selection account directly answered the composition objection by identifying a purposeless process capable of generating organized biological functions.
The compatibilist account specified autonomy, self-control, and robust abilities as responsibility-relevant capacities, offering a substantive alternative to libertarian indeterminism.
The matched-robot thought experiment sharply demonstrated that bare randomness adds no evident control, trustworthiness, or responsibility to an otherwise equivalent system.
The levels-of-explanation distinction provided the most comprehensive reply, showing that explanatory autonomy does not by itself entail additional metaphysical ingredients.
The constructed-yet-discoverable chess example effectively defeated the narrow inference from discovery to independence from human practices.

blunders.text: The mortality and robot discussion shifted among reproducibility, immortality, contracts, vulnerability, and personhood without directly answering the persisting-subject or agent-choice arguments.
The broad claim that naturalism adequately explains every listed human phenomenon was asserted more expansively than the selected mechanisms and qualifications supported.
The vitalism analogy was diagnostically useful but did not establish that phenomenal consciousness relates to cognitive capacities exactly as discarded vital forces related to biological processes.

newArguments.title: Contrastive realization test
newArguments.text: A stronger pro methodology would compare rival realization theories using contrastive cases. If two systems share every proposed functional, behavioral, computational, and relational property, the pro side should ask whether the theories nevertheless permit a difference in experience, normative authority, or ownership. If they do, the realization base is incomplete by the theory's own lights; if they do not, the pro side can demand an explanation of why the identity is necessary rather than stipulated. This test converts a general intuition about irreducibility into a focused burden for competing accounts.

novelty.explanation: This is a new methodological argument using contrastive theory testing rather than repeating any participant's live claim.

newArguments.title: Normative error constraint
newArguments.text: A naturalized value account must explain not only agreement and improvement within practices but also the possibility that an entire settled practice is unjust. The pro side can argue that practice-independent standards earn explanatory work when they make systematic moral error intelligible without reducing error to inconsistency with another local convention. This does not establish a supernatural source of value; it instead places a precise adequacy constraint on constructivist theories and leaves open several realist ontologies compatible with the limited irreducibility thesis.

novelty.explanation: This develops the value exchange into a whole-practice error test while keeping the conclusion proportionate.

newArguments.title: Intervention convergence argument
newArguments.text: Naturalism gains support when independently targeted interventions converge on the same organized capacities. Changes to neural circuitry, development, learning environments, and social scaffolding can each alter memory continuity, purposive planning, moral sensitivity, and self-control in predictable ways. Convergence would be difficult to explain if the decisive personal properties belonged primarily to an independent subject whose relation to these interventions remained unspecified. The inference is defeasible, but it gives naturalism a comparative evidential advantage and identifies what an irreducibility theory must explain rather than relying solely on methodological optimism.

novelty.explanation: This is a new comparative inference from convergent interventions across several person-level capacities.

newArguments.title: Cross-level causal stability
newArguments.text: Higher-level properties earn realism when they support stable counterfactuals across many physical implementations. A promise, goal, belief, or autonomous policy can explain behavior even when its neural details vary, because changing the higher-level state would predictably change action across realizations. Naturalism can therefore preserve causal significance without requiring fundamental particles to contain promises or purposes. This answers the catalogue objection more directly than simple analogy: explanatory autonomy reflects robust organization and counterfactual structure, while metaphysical addition would require separate evidence beyond the usefulness of the higher-level description.

novelty.explanation: This develops the levels reply into a counterfactual criterion for genuine higher-level causal explanation.
